title: The robot
drafted: By hand, as a proposal, on 2026-11-24. No model was asked. Nothing here is canon until you choose.

breakdown.logline: A small, earnest robot who has just come out of a capsule and wants very much to be useful.
breakdown.essence: Kind, eager and a little old-fashioned, like a tin toy that has read a manual on manners. Takes every job seriously, however small. Not a menace and not a joke: the cast should be glad it came.
breakdown.look: A toy-shop robot, not a factory one. A boxy head a bit too big for it, two round lamp eyes and a grille for a mouth on a dark face plate. A barrel chest with one round red dial in the middle. Short round arms and legs with a ball at every elbow, knee, shoulder and hip. Mitten hands. Wide flat feet. Painted enamel, not chrome.
breakdown.silhouette: A box on a barrel on two short posts. At a glance from across the stage it is the only square head in the cast, and the shortest figure: it should never be mistaken for anyone else, even as a few dozen pixels.
breakdown.height_why: The shortest in the line-up (the dancer is 1.65, the villager 1.7, Lincoln 1.93), so it reads as new and young, and its big head keeps a face you can find from the crew camera.

breakdown.palette_why: Nobody in the cast wears yellow. Three of them wear navy (Roosevelt's singlet, the pirate's coat, the ninja), three wear browns and linens (Lincoln, the villager, the lizardkin's leathers), two are green (the troll, the lizardkin) and the dancer has the red. Mustard stands apart from all of them in hue and is far lighter than the navies, so the height line-up reads at once. The joints take the brand's steel blue, a calmer blue than the navies. One small red dial is the only accent.
reads_as_cards: Rigid parts, one a bone: a robot's forearm really is one stiff piece, so a card of it is the truth and not a trick. Nothing stretches at a joint.
Real ball joints, the size of the joint, where the cards already put a ball. What the cards fill a bent joint with is what the robot is made of.
Matte enamel. A shine is baked into each picture and jumps when the card swaps to the next one; flat paint does not.
Big flat areas of few colours: the pixel sheet keeps 32 colours and this needs five.
Nothing that hangs or swings: no cables, no antenna on a spring, no cape. Loose things are where cards come apart.
reads_in_bold_ink: A clean outline: square head, round chest, posts for limbs. Bold ink draws its thick line round exactly that.
A panel seam round the chest and the head's edge give the thin inner lines something true to follow.
Lamp eyes are light on dark, so the hard shadow edge never swallows them.
reads_in_pixels_both: Eyes big enough to survive: each about a quarter of the face's width, so three to four of the big pixels from the crew camera, where an eye on the current cast gets two and a half to three and a half.
A grille of three bars for a mouth, each bar a whole pixel at the head's finer grid.
Head turns read as a box turning, which a few pixels can show and a nose cannot.
must_have: Drawn in a T-pose, front on, arms straight out, empty hands, as every character picture is.
Two round lamp eyes and a grille mouth on a dark face plate, head level, looking straight ahead.
A visible ball at each shoulder, elbow, hip and knee.
Wide flat feet that can hold a deep squat.
Matte painted enamel in the palette above.
must_not: Chrome, glass domes, screens or lights that glow (TRELLIS builds glass badly, and a glow is a shine).
Thin wires, antennae, springs, tubes, fingers.
Text, numbers or logos painted on.
Anything held. Props are made on their own afterwards.
Weapons, or a menacing face. This is a gentle cast.
breakdown.in_the_ensemble: Lincoln is patient and tall, Roosevelt is all energy, the pirate is practical, the ninja watches. The robot is the eager newcomer who asks everyone how things are done, and gets three different answers. It gives Lincoln someone to tell long stories to, Roosevelt someone to race, the pirate a pair of hands for the ropes, and the ninja a new face to frame.
breakdown.the_sides_it_must_pass: The deep squat (knees), the head turn (the neck, still being worked on) and the arm overhead (the shoulder) are where the current cast's cards are weakest; a robot built of real balls and posts should score better than any of them there. If it does not, that is a note for the cards, not for the robot.

canon_options.name: The developer's helper
canon_options.pitch: It drops out of the gachapon holding nothing, and believes it was sent by the developer to finish the world: it goes looking for every "TODO" it can find, starting with the sign at the corner of the map. Nobody has the heart to tell it that it is a toon like the rest of them.
canon_options.who_paid: Nobody it knows of. A capsule nobody ordered: the first pull the gachapon ever made on its own. (For us: the credits were spent, as always; in the story, it is a wondrous accident.)
canon_options.where: It sleeps standing up beside the gachapon at the spawn spot, so it can greet whoever comes next.
canon_options.touches: Plays on the premise (a world being built a little at a time) without explaining it. Gives the "TODO: more world" corner and the Niantic someone who wants to go there.

canon_options.name: Lincoln's counter
canon_options.pitch: Lincoln has wanted an honest shop for a while ("Lincoln's counter", not yet seen). He saves up and pulls a capsule, and out comes a clerk: a robot that counts change to the penny and walks the miles with him to give it back. Lincoln treats it as a partner, never as a machine.
canon_options.who_paid: Lincoln, from credits saved over many strips.
canon_options.where: Behind the counter of Lincoln's shop, once there is one; until then, at his side.
canon_options.touches: Brings a "not yet seen" idea onto the page, and shows Lincoln at his warmest: patient, honest, teaching. Needs care that the shop is about honesty and kindness, never about politics.

canon_options.name: The Square Deal crew's first hire
canon_options.pitch: Roosevelt and the pirate pool what they have to get a builder for the Square Deal Construction Company (not yet seen), and the gachapon gives them a robot. It is short, earnest and stronger than it looks: it lifts the giant baguette into place for the boarding house while the two of them argue about where it goes.
canon_options.where: The settlement's edge, in the site hut beside the baguette boarding house.
canon_options.touches: Gives the audition's lifts and squats a story reason. Brings the Square Deal company and the baguette boarding house onto the page.

canon_options.name: Brewed in the teahouse
canon_options.pitch: The first toon made through the troll's teahouse (not yet seen): someone ordered a new self at the character screen, it was sealed in a pearl and dropped into the gachapon, and came back out believing it is a robot. It is quite sure about this. The troll is quietly proud.
canon_options.who_paid: Unknown: whoever stood at the teahouse screen, which is a mystery the strips can keep.
canon_options.where: The settlement, helping at the troll and lizardkin's stall.
canon_options.touches: Opens the teahouse and the pearl, two ideas under "Not yet seen", in one arrival. Fits "believes they are who they ordered" exactly.

looks.name: Tin toy
looks.why: The plainest reading of the breakdown: a wind-up toy robot, the kind that walks across a table.

brief.name: Tin Toy Robot
brief.description: A small friendly robot built like an old wind-up tin toy: a boxy head, a barrel chest and short round limbs with a ball at every joint. Painted matte mustard and steel blue, about the height of a twelve-year-old.
brief.subject: A small friendly toy robot standing in a T-pose. A boxy head, slightly too big, with a flat charcoal face plate, two large round cream-coloured lamp eyes and a mouth grille of three horizontal bars. A short round neck collar. A barrel-shaped chest in matte mustard-yellow enamel with one round tomato-red dial in the middle and a raised seam around it. Upper arms and thighs are mustard cylinders; forearms and shins are steel-blue cylinders; a steel-blue ball sits at each shoulder, elbow, hip and knee. Charcoal mitten hands and wide flat charcoal feet. A chunky mustard wind-up key with two round wings fixed to the middle of its back. Matte painted enamel everywhere, lightly worn at the edges; no chrome, no glass, no text.

brief.name: Builder Robot
brief.description: A short, sturdy builder robot: a boxy head under a round hard hat, a broad barrel chest, thick limbs with ball joints, a tool belt and wide feet. Matte mustard and steel-blue paint.
brief.subject: A short, sturdy builder robot standing in a T-pose. A boxy head with a flat charcoal face plate, two large round cream-coloured lamp eyes and a mouth grille of three horizontal bars, under a round steel-blue hard hat with a small brim that leaves the eyes clear. A broad barrel chest in matte mustard-yellow enamel with one round tomato-red dial. Thick upper arms and thighs in mustard; thick forearms and shins in steel blue; a steel-blue ball at each shoulder, elbow, hip and knee. A plain charcoal tool belt with two closed pouches, close to the waist. Charcoal mitten hands and very wide flat charcoal feet. Matte painted enamel, a little scuffed; no chrome, no glass, no text.
